subject: Post-call: Anka Health pricing guardrails & target $/1M tokens
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@anka.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + ask: volumes, budget range, target $/1M tokens

Hi Maya — thanks again for the demo and the honest discussion earlier. Quick recap and two requests so we can map a pricing proposal to Anka's economics.

Call highlights (TL;DR):
- Primary workload: NLU generation for triage + patient messaging (low-latency, steady QPS).
- Expected steady-state volume: roughly 5–10M generated tokens/month.
- Embeddings: ~50k vectors/month for search and similarity.
- Priority: keep unit costs predictable; prefer committed pricing if it moves us below OPEX thresholds.

A. Pricing ask (what we need from you):
1) Can you confirm the target budget range for model inference (monthly)? You mentioned a preliminary ops budget of ~$10–20k/month — is that across all AI infra or only LLM inference?
2) Target $/1M tokens: do you have a target price (benchmark) you want us to meet or beat vs OpenAI/Anthropic/other hosts? If you can share a ballpark ($/1M), we can propose realistic model tiers.

B. What we'll send:
- An initial pricing grid with per-1M-token bands (hosted vs dedicated) and model-equivalent examples (we'll include rough comparable numbers for OpenAI and Anthropic).
- A short committed-capacity outline (how much discount at 3/6/12 month commits).

Attachments: Anka_RFP_Q1.pdf (your RFP from today) — I attached the call notes, plus our draft pricing grid (redwood-token-pricing-grid.xlsx).

Next steps: if you can confirm the two asks above by EOD Thursday (your timezone), I will route a tailored pricing + technical POC plan to Procurement and copy Rishi for SLAs/security scope.

Thanks — appreciate the transparency here.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

From: Maya Singh <maya@anka.health>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Ops (Anka) <sourcing@anka.health>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: volumes, budget range, target $/1M tokens

Thanks Vanessa — good to get this in writing. Quick answers and some context from procurement side.

1) Budget: the $10–20k/month I mentioned was for initial proof-of-value (pilot) only. If the economics scale, there is a separate infra budget that could expand to $40–60k/mo for inference, but Procurement needs a clear $/1M token target to evaluate TCO vs our current vendor.

2) Target $/1M tokens: our internal target benchmark to be competitive for this use case is roughly $1,200/1M generated tokens (this is what our finance team flagged as a threshold to keep unit economics healthy). For embeddings we'd like something in the $150–300/100k-embedding range, but embeddings are a lower portion of spend.

Model preferences / constraints:
- We prefer an open-model option (quantized) if it meets latency and quality — it materially impacts unit cost.
- If there is a meaningful quality delta for Anthropic/OpenAI models that matters to clinical safety, we would consider paying up, but Procurement will need a clear delta justification.

Attachment: I attached our procurement intake (included in Anka_RFP_Q1.pdf). Next: can you send that pricing grid with short comparative notes vs OpenAI/Anthropic? Procurement will want line-item numbers to plug into their TCO spreadsheet.

Best,
Maya

Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: volumes, budget range, target $/1M tokens

Maya — thanks for the clarity. I wanted to give a short, pragmatic mapping from Redwood's side so Procurement has apples-to-apples numbers to run in the TCO sheet. Below are conservative per-1M-token examples — these are illustrative, final numbers depend on model selection, sequence length, and whether you choose hosted vs Dedicated commit.

Redwood hosted (no commit) — typical comparators: quantized open models (Llama2 family / community-verified weights):
- Estimated: $1,800 — $2,400 per 1M generated tokens (small seq lengths, micro-batched).
- Embeddings (100k vectors): $250 — $350 equivalent (back-of-envelope).

Redwood hosted (volume discounts at 5–10M tokens/mo):
- Estimated: $1,200 — $1,600 per 1M generated tokens (depending on QPS profile).

Redwood dedicated (reserved GPU pools, 6–12mo commit):
- Estimated committed price: $450 — $700 per 1M generated tokens (this is where committed capacity materially beats public-host pricing).

Comparative benchmarks (public market, approximate list pricing we use for TCO):
- OpenAI (gpt-4-style or latest gen) equivalent: $3,500 — $8,000 / 1M tokens (higher for 4-style; 3.5 lower).
- Anthropic (Claude-like): $2,200 — $4,500 / 1M tokens.
- Other open-model hosts (managed Llama2, Mistral forks): $1,300 — $2,500 / 1M tokens (varies by quantization/support).

Key notes for Procurement to consider:
- Quality vs price: open-model quantized stacks get you closer to your $1,200 target if you take Dedicated commits. If your target is strict for hosted (no commit) we will likely be above $1,200/1M unless you accept model/latency tradeoffs.
- SLA & security delta: Dedicated + Private deployment give you SOC2 logs, VPC, KMS integration — Procurement often budgets ~10–20% premium for those controls.
- Switching cost & fallbacks: We support auto-fallback to higher-capacity variants if traffic spikes; we can show simulated monthly spend under different failure scenarios.

Proposed next steps (short):
1) Vanessa to send the hosted vs committed pricing grid (done) + 1-pager on model-quality tradeoffs for clinical NLU.
2) Anka to confirm whether $1,200/1M is a hard procurement requirement for hosted mode or negotiable only with commit.
3) If commit is possible, we (Redwood) will run a 2-week POC with a capped spend to demonstrate latency and token accounting.

I attached rdw-commit-tier-outline.pdf with mapped discounts per commit level. Monica — can you help prep a one-pager on expected latency and token yield differences between our recommended quantized open-model stack and Anthropic/OpenAI equivalents? I'll pull together a short example TCO tab that aligns to Anka's numbers.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai
